mainTopic: The end of the לחם הפנים question and the day counts for eating שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים; then the new chapter on redeeming מנחות and נסכים before and after a כלי
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about לחם הפנים left on the שולחן into Friday night: shouldn't the שולחן consecrate it and then make it disqualified? רבא answers that the כהן took the loaves off before nightfall. מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) answers that bread arranged the wrong way is like bread arranged by a monkey, so the שולחן never consecrates it. A new משנה then teaches that שתי הלחם are eaten two or three days after baking, and לחם הפנים nine to eleven days after baking. The reason is that baking them does not override שבת or יום טוב, though רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that it does override יום טוב. רבינא uses this to prove that, according to the view that forbids them, נדרים ונדבות are unfit on יום טוב by Torah law. The chapter שתי הלחם ends, and a new chapter begins: טמא מנחות and נסכים can be redeemed before a כלי makes them holy, but not after. שמואל says even pure ones can be redeemed before a כלי. The גמרא explains why the משנה still had to state that items made holy in a כלי can't be redeemed, since a בעל מום is called 'טמא'. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Shouldn't the loaves become consecrated at twilight and then disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: when Friday night's twilight arrives, the loaves still on the שולחן should become consecrated and then disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the night comes, at twilight, the bread should become consecrated and then become disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the case of the earlier משנה. If the night before the proper time is not considered 'too early,' the loaves sitting on the שולחן should get consecrated at Friday's twilight and then become invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge builds on the idea that night does not count as 'before its time.' If so, once Friday-night twilight arrives, the שולחן should consecrate the loaves already on it. After that they would become disqualified, which clashes with the משנה's ruling. The question puts pressure on how that case actually worked.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the in-between time at nightfall (בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת)
Night
Let it become consecrated (by the שולחן)
Let it become disqualified

phrases.english: When the night arrives, the twilight [of Shabbat eve],
let it be consecrated and then disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מָטֵי לֵילְיָא דְּבֵי שִׁימְשֵׁי לִיקְדּוֹשׁ וְלִיפְּסוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether night counts as 'before its time' for the שולחן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier משנה's ruling about loaves arranged after שבת and left on the שולחן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If night is not 'too early,' the שולחן should consecrate the loaves at Friday twilight. Then they would become disqualified, which does not fit the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: the כהן removed the loaves before nightfall
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the case is one where the כהן took the loaves off the שולחן before Friday night came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is talking about where he removed it beforehand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The כהן removed the bread before twilight, so it was never on the שולחן when night came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the loaves are still on the שולחן at twilight. רבא says the משנה is speaking about a כהן who took them off first, so nothing could become consecrated. He then arranged them again the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted first, before (the night came)
He removed (the loaves from the שולחן)
The golden Table in the היכל, which consecrates the bread placed on it

phrases.english: Rava says: [It is] where he removed [it] beforehand.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the loaves were still on the שולחן at Friday twilight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן removed them before nightfall, so the שולחן never consecrated them.

steps.title: Bread arranged the wrong way is like bread arranged by a monkey
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) says that even if the bread was not removed, it does not become consecrated, because arranging it against the מצוה counts as if a monkey arranged it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, and some say רב אשי, said: You can even say he did not remove it beforehand. Since he arranged it not according to its מצוה, it is as if a monkey arranged it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer is given that does not need רבא's narrow case. Bread placed on the שולחן in an improper way does not count as a real arrangement, so the שולחן cannot consecrate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needed the loaves to be off the שולחן. This answer says that even if they stayed on, it makes no difference. Since the arrangement was done שלא כמצותו, it has no legal value, like a monkey putting bread on a table. So there is nothing for the שולחן to consecrate.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (introduces an answer that works even without the earlier limit)
Not in the way the מצוה requires
Monkey; an act with no legal meaning

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: רבא says the loaves were taken off before night. מר זוטרא/רב אשי says that even on the שולחן they are not consecrated, because an improper arrangement is like a monkey's.

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, and some say Rav Ashi, said:
Even if you say [it is] where he did not remove [it] beforehand,
since he arranged it not in accordance with its מצוה,
it is as though a monkey had arranged it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 1 that does not depend on רבא's narrowing of the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle-based answer: an improper act has no legal effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רבא's limit, the loaves on the שולחן would become consecrated at twilight.
steps.terutzMaskana: An arrangement done שלא כמצותו is like a monkey's, so the שולחן never consecrates the loaves.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'monkey' idea teaches that a מצוה act done improperly can be treated as if it never happened at all, and not just as a flawed act.

steps.title: New משנה: שתי הלחם are eaten two or three days after baking
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that the two loaves of שבועות are eaten no fewer than two and no more than three days after they are baked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two loaves are eaten no less than two days and no more than three. How? They are baked on ערב יום טוב and eaten on יום טוב, the second day. If יום טוב falls after שבת, they are eaten on the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the timing for eating שתי הלחם of שבועות, counting from the day they were baked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the loaves are baked the day before יום טוב and eaten on יום טוב, so the eating falls on the second day counting the baking day. When שבועות falls on Sunday, they cannot be baked on שבת, so they are baked Friday and eaten on the third day.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of a new משנה
The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות
How so? (introduces the explanation of a rule)
The day before the festival

steps.confusionAlert: The counting includes the day of baking. Baked Thursday and eaten Friday counts as 'the second day,' not 'one day later.'

phrases.english: MISHNA: The two loaves are eaten

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם, וְלֹא יוֹתֵר עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: no less than two [days] and no more than three.
How so? They are baked on the eve of the Festival
and eaten on the Festival, on the second [day].

phrases.aramaic: חָל יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת –
phrases.english: If the Festival occurs after Shabbat,
they are eaten on the third [day].
phrases.notes: They can't be baked on שבת, so they're baked Friday and eaten Sunday.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם נֶאֱכָלוֹת אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins on a new topic: the timing of eating the breads.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שתי הלחם are eaten on the second day after baking, or on the third day when שבועות falls on Sunday.

steps.title: לחם הפנים is eaten nine to eleven days after baking
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: לחם הפנים is eaten no fewer than nine and no more than eleven days after baking. Normally that is the ninth day, and the tenth when יום טוב falls on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לחם הפנים is eaten no less than nine days and no more than eleven. How? It is baked on ערב שבת and eaten on the next שבת, the ninth day. If יום טוב falls on ערב שבת, it is eaten on the tenth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the same kind of timing rule for לחם הפנים. It explains the normal nine-day case and the ten-day case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread is baked Friday, placed on the שולחן on שבת, and eaten the following שבת. Counting the baking day, that is the ninth day. If Friday is יום טוב, the baking moves to Thursday, so the eating falls on the tenth day. The eleven-day case is explained right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread: twelve loaves arranged each שבת on the שולחן
Friday, the day before שבת
It falls (on a certain day)

phrases.english: The shewbread is eaten

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פָּחוֹת מִתִּשְׁעָה, וְלֹא יוֹתֵר עַל אַחַד עָשָׂר.
phrases.english: no less than nine [days] and no more than eleven.
How so? It is baked on Shabbat eve
and eaten on [the following] Shabbat, on the ninth [day].

phrases.aramaic: חָל יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת –
phrases.english: If a Festival occurs on Shabbat eve,
it is eaten on the tenth [day].

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים נֶאֱכָל אֵין פָּחוֹת מִתִּשְׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from שתי הלחם to לחם הפנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לחם הפנים is normally eaten on the ninth day after baking, and on the tenth when יום טוב falls on Friday.
steps.whatToRemember: Both breads are counted from the day of baking. שתי הלחם: 2 to 3 days. לחם הפנים: 9 to 11 days. The baking is pushed earlier when שבת or יום טוב gets in the way.

steps.title: After the two days of ראש השנה, the bread is eaten on the eleventh day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the longest case: when the two days of ראש השנה come right before שבת, the לחם הפנים is eaten eleven days after baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the two festival days of ראש השנה come before שבת, the bread is eaten on the eleventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of how many days can pass between baking the לחם הפנים and eating it, and gives the eleven-day case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread is normally baked on Friday. If ראש השנה falls on Thursday and Friday, the baking must move back to Wednesday. The bread is placed on the שולחן that שבת and eaten the שבת after, so counting from Wednesday to that second שבת gives eleven days. That is the maximum mentioned in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year festival, which lasts two days
Festival days, when ordinary work such as baking is restricted
On the eleventh day

phrases.english: The two festival days of Rosh HaShana:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording. Picture ראש השנה on Thursday and Friday, so the baking moves back to Wednesday.

phrases.english: it is eaten on the eleventh day.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the eleven-day case to the nine- and ten-day cases listed in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the two days of ראש השנה come before שבת, the לחם הפנים is eaten on the eleventh day after baking.

steps.title: Baking the breads does not override שבת or יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the reason for all these delays: preparing the breads does not push aside שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the preparation of the breads does not override שבת, and it does not override יום טוב either.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rule behind the whole day count: the breads cannot be baked on שבת or יום טוב, so they are baked earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why the eating day can be the tenth or eleventh day instead of the ninth. The baking must move earlier to avoid a holy day, while the eating day stays the same. The rule covers both the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Overrides, pushes aside (a prohibition)
The Sabbath
A festival day

steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא's proof in the גמרא (Step 10) is built on exactly this line.

phrases.english: And it does not override Shabbat
phrases.notes: "It" means baking and preparing the breads.

phrases.english: and not a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ דּוֹחֶה לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the day counts in Steps 4 through 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparing the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים overrides neither שבת nor יום טוב.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: it overrides יום טוב but not the fast day
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, quoting רבי שמעון בן הסגן, disagrees and says the baking does override יום טוב, but not יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי שמעון בן הסגן: it overrides יום טוב, but it does not override the fast day.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה disagrees with the rule we just read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, baking the breads is allowed on יום טוב, so it would not have to move earlier because of a festival. It still may not be done on יום כיפור. The disagreement is only about יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy כהן גדול
The fast day, meaning יום כיפור

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon, son of the deputy High Priest:
It overrides a Festival,
but it does not override the fast day.
phrases.notes: The fast day here is יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן הַסְּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's rule in Step 7 about יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparing the breads overrides יום טוב but not יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבינא: נדרים ונדבות are unfit on יום טוב even from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that the opinion forbidding נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב holds that this is a Torah-level rule, not just a rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: according to the one who says נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב, don't think that by Torah law they are fit and the רבנן forbade them so that people would not delay. Rather, even by Torah law they are not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רבינא's claim about why some hold that voluntary offerings may not be brought on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the ban is only a rabbinic decree, so that people would not hold off bringing their offerings until the festival. רבינא says no: according to this view, the Torah itself makes them unfit on יום טוב. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow offerings and voluntary offerings, which are not required on a specific day
By Torah law
They (the רבנן) decreed
He will delay

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not ruling on the הלכה himself. He is explaining the reasoning of "the one who says" these offerings are not brought on יום טוב.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ravina said:
According to the statement of the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: vow offerings and voluntary offerings are not sacrificed on a Festival,
do not say that by Torah law they are fit,
and it is the Sages who decreed, so that one would not delay,
phrases.notes: The worry is that a person would hold off bringing his offering until he came up to ירושלים for the festival.

phrases.english: rather, by Torah law too they are not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a claim that will be proven from the משנה's rule in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the view forbidding נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב, they are unfit מדאורייתא, not only because of a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: The proof: even the required שתי הלחם do not override יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבינא proves his point: the שתי הלחם are required on that day, so there is no worry about delay, and yet the משנה says they do not override יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the שתי הלחם are an obligation of the day, so we cannot say the reason is "lest he delay," and yet the משנה teaches that they do not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings his proof from the משנה in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "don't delay" decree cannot apply to the שתי הלחם, because they must be brought on שבועות anyway. Even so, the משנה says preparing them does not override יום טוב, so the reason must be a Torah-level one. If a required offering is held back by the Torah, then optional נדרים ונדבות certainly are.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves offered on שבועות
An obligation of the day, required on that specific day
And yet it teaches (in the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Even a required offering like the שתי הלחם does not override יום טוב (according to the תנא קמא). So the ban on נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב is from the Torah, not a rabbinic decree against delay.

phrases.english: For the two loaves
are an obligation of the day,
and one cannot say "lest he delay,"
and yet the mishna teaches: it does not override

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: neither Shabbat nor a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם דְּחוֹבַת הַיּוֹם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רבינא's claim in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That נדרים ונדבות are unfit on יום טוב מדאורייתא according to the view that forbids them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (Step 7): preparing the שתי הלחם, an obligation of the day with no worry of delay, still does not override יום טוב.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The chapter שתי הלחם ends with the traditional farewell line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter שתי הלחם.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line marking the end of the chapter שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no new argument here. It is a formula of parting from the chapter and expressing hope to come back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The Two Loaves."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after רבינא's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter שתי הלחם is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: redeeming טמא מנחות and נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that טמא מנחות and נסכים can be redeemed before they are made holy in a כלי, but not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meal offerings and wine offerings that became impure can be redeemed if they were not yet made holy in a sacred vessel. Once they were made holy in a vessel, they cannot be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about whether מנחות and נסכים that became טמא can be redeemed for money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on one moment: being placed in a כלי שרת. Before that moment, redemption is possible. After it, redemption is not possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: moving the holiness onto money so the item becomes ordinary
Wine offerings poured on the altar
Became holy by being placed in a sacred vessel
Became ritually impure

phrases.english: MISHNA: The meal offerings and the libations
that became impure, before they were consecrated in a vessel
they have redemption;
once they were consecrated in a vessel, they have no redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the closing line of שתי הלחם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טמא מנחות and נסכים are redeemable only before they are made holy in a כלי.

steps.title: Birds, wood, frankincense and vessels can never be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists items that cannot be redeemed even when טמא, because the Torah mentions redemption only for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds, wood, frankincense and sacred vessels that became impure cannot be redeemed, because the Torah speaks of redemption only for an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second group of holy items that can never be redeemed, and gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason comes from the Torah's wording: redemption is mentioned only for a בהמה. So these other altar items stay holy even when they become טמא and unusable.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense
Sacred vessels used in the Temple service
An animal (a large or small domesticated animal)

phrases.english: The birds, the wood, the frankincense and the service vessels,
once they became impure, they have no redemption,
for redemption was stated only regarding an animal.

steps.whatToRemember: For altar items, the Torah mentions redemption only for an animal. מנחות and נסכים are different only before a כלי makes them holy.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a contrasting list of items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds, wood, לבונה and כלי שרת are never redeemable, even when טמא.

steps.title: שמואל: even טהור מנחות can be redeemed before a כלי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that even טהור מנחות and נסכים may be redeemed before being placed in a כלי, because until then they have only קדושת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: even if they are pure, they can be redeemed. Why? As long as they were not made holy in a vessel, their holiness is only on their value, and such holiness can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with שמואל, who widens the משנה's first ruling to include pure מנחות as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the כלי, the flour or wine is holy only for its money value (קדושת דמים), and that kind of holiness can be moved onto money. So whether it is טמא or not makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness on an item's value only, which can be redeemed
Ritually pure
Are redeemed
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
Even if they are pure, they are redeemed.
phrases.notes: "They" means the מנחות and נסכים from the משנה, before they were put in a כלי.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
As long as they were not consecrated in a vessel,
they have sanctity of value,
and things with sanctity of value are redeemed.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: if purity makes no difference, why does the משנה say "that became impure"?
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וַאֲפִילּוּ הֵן טְהוֹרִין נִפְדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the first ruling of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before a כלי makes them holy, even טהור מנחות and נסכים can be redeemed, because they only have קדושת דמים.

steps.title: But the משנה says they became impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the משנה specifically speaks of items that became טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה, "that became impure"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pure items could also be redeemed, the משנה would not need to say "that became impure." That wording seems to suggest that only טמא items can be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in the משנה (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But we learned "became impure"?

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that טהור items are also redeemable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words "that became impure" suggest that redemption depends on being טמא.

steps.title: "Impure" was mentioned only to match the second half
steps.stepSummary: The same law applies to pure items. The משנה said טמא in the first half only to match the second half, which teaches that after a כלי even a טמא item cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even if they did not become impure. But since the משנה wanted to teach in the second half that once they are made holy in a vessel they cannot be redeemed, even if they became impure, it also taught the first half with "became impure, before they were made holy in a vessel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by explaining why the משנה used the word "impure" in its first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "impure" is really needed in the second half. There it teaches a big point: even a disqualified, טמא item cannot be redeemed after a כלי. The first half used the same wording just so the two halves would match, not to limit the law.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
Since; because (one half was worded to match the other)
The latter clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the word "impure" in the first half as a requirement. It is there only because of the matching wording; pure מנחות are redeemable too.
steps.whatToRemember: Before a כלי: redeemable, whether טמא or טהור. After a כלי: never redeemable, not even when טמא.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נִטְמְאוּ,
phrases.english: The same is true even though they did not become impure,
but since it wants to teach the latter clause:
"Once they were consecrated in a vessel, they have no redemption,"
meaning that even if they became impure, also not,
it also taught the first clause
"that became impure, before they were consecrated in a vessel."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נִטְמְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and upholds שמואל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word "impure" in the first half limits redemption to טמא items.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "impure" is needed only for the second half's point. The first half copies it for matching wording, so pure items are also redeemable before a כלי.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that items holy in a כלי can't be redeemed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה had to teach that items made holy in a כלי cannot be redeemed. They have קדושת הגוף, so that should be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! They have holiness of the body itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the משנה. Why tell us something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a מנחה or נסך is placed in a כלי שרת, the item itself becomes holy (קדושת הגוף), not just its money value. Items with קדושת הגוף are never redeemed. So the גמרא asks what the משנה is adding by saying it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. A challenge asking why a source bothered to state something clear.
Holiness of the item itself, which cannot be redeemed (as opposed to holiness of its money value).

phrases.english: It is obvious, they have holiness of the body!
phrases.notes: "They" means the מנחות and נסכים that were already made holy in a כלי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 16 explained that the second half of the משנה teaches that even a טמא item cannot be redeemed after a כלי. Now the גמרא asks why that even needed saying.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that מנחות and נסכים made holy in a כלי cannot be redeemed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items with קדושת הגוף can obviously never be redeemed, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: It was needed, because a בעל מום is called טמא
steps.stepSummary: The ruling was needed. Since the Torah calls a בעל מום 'טמא', we might have compared a טמא item to a בעל מום and allowed it to be redeemed. The משנה teaches that this comparison is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: since a blemished animal is called 'impure,' an impure item is also like a blemished animal. A blemished animal is redeemed when it gets a blemish, even though it has holiness of the body. So these items should also be redeemed. The משנה teaches us that this is not the kind of 'impure' the Torah meant when it called a blemished animal 'impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a mistake we could have made. The משנה needed to block that mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום is the one case where something with קדושת הגוף can still be redeemed. Because the Torah calls a בעל מום 'טמא', we might have said every טמא holy item works the same way. The משנה tells us the Torah's word 'טמא' for a בעל מום does not mean actual טומאה, so a טמא מנחה in a כלי stays unredeemable.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary. The standard way of answering a פשיטא challenge.
It might enter your mind to say. This introduces the mistaken first thought (הוה אמינא).
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be offered and may be redeemed.
It teaches us. This introduces what the source really comes to teach.
The Merciful One. A way of referring to God or the Torah.

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל מום is called 'טמא' in the Torah, but that is a different sense of the word. Real טומאה does not let a holy item in a כלי be redeemed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a בעל מום is ritually impure. The Torah's word 'טמא' for it is a separate use of the word, and that is exactly the point the משנה is teaching.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
it might enter your mind to say:
since a blemished animal is called "impure,"
an impure item is also similar to a blemished animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף,
phrases.english: and even though it is holy with holiness of the body,
when a blemish develops in it, it is redeemed,
so these too should be redeemed.
phrases.notes: "These" are the טמא מנחות and נסכים that were already made holy in a כלי.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that it is not like this "impure"
that the Merciful One called a blemished animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the פשיטא challenge of step 17 by showing a mistake the משנה needed to prevent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling was needed to block a mistaken comparison (איצטריך).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah calls a בעל מום 'טמא', a טמא holy item could be treated like a בעל מום and redeemed despite its קדושת הגוף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah's word 'טמא' for a בעל מום is not this kind of טומאה, so a טמא item made holy in a כלי cannot be redeemed.
